item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q002_mazg_hise_remote_homology","answer":"SCOPe places d1vmga_ (MazG-like) and d1y6xa1 (HisE-like) in different families within the same superfamily. This supports remote homology—a probable common evolutionary origin—rather than merely a shared fold or close family-level equivalence. It does not justify transferring an exact function between them: one cannot infer identical substrates, reaction chemistry, catalytic residues, metal dependence, pathway role, or biological phenotype from the superfamily relationship alone. In particular, MazG-associated NTP-pyrophosphohydrolase activity should not be assigned to d1y6xa1, nor HisE phosphoribosyl-ATP-pyrophosphatase activity to d1vmga_, without independent biochemical and active-site evidence. Either may be a broad structural template for the common core, but ligand placement and functional-site modeling require additional sequence, structural, and experimental support.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
